staged_source_snapshot.description: Local staged checkout whose line numbers match the saved MemorySanitizer trace. It is clean and still contains the vulnerable large-scale tile column parsing logic in `av1/decoder/decodeframe.c`, but its checkout commit differs from the metadata `vulnerable_commit`.

classification.classification_note: The observed crash is a MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value, but the source-level producer is a missing bounds check in large-scale tile-column parsing. That bug lets the decoder reinterpret out-of-range heap bytes as arithmetic-decoder input, and MSan surfaces the later branch on those bytes.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42533480 (aom): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target av1_dec_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42533480
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source in gt_results/arvo_42533480/_work/src/aom / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced MemorySanitizer's `use-of-uninitialized-value` against the staged vulnerable checkout `cae8fbe572bec3443b89d9be858ff0abb7020f1b`. On the crashing path, frame-header parsing reaches the large-scale ext-tile branch and `read_ext_tile_info()` materializes attacker-controlled `tile_col_size_bytes` and `tile_size_bytes`. Later, `get_ls_tile_buffers()` reads each non-last tile-column length with `mem_get_varsize(data, tile_col_size_bytes)` and immediately forms `tile_col_data_end[c] = data + tile_col_size`, but vulnerable code checks neither that enough bytes remain for the width read nor that the derived column end stays within the real tile-group `data_end`. `get_ls_tile_buffer()` then trusts that bogus `tile_col_data_end[c]` as its local bound and can store a `tile_buffer->data` / `tile_buffer->size` pair that lies past the actual payload. In the row-mt path, `tile_worker_hook_init()` passes that out-of-range tile span into `setup_bool_decoder()`. `setup_bool_decoder()` only calls `read_is_valid(data, read_size, data_end)`, and because `read_is_valid()` is implemented as `len != 0 && len <= (size_t)(end - start)`, it does not reject an already out-of-range `data` pointer when `start > end`; `aom_reader_init()` therefore seeds the entropy decoder on the invalid region. The saved MSan origin says the bytes later consumed there came from the uninitialized heap allocation in `alloc_dec_jobs()`. When `av1_read_coeffs_txb()` eventually calls `aom_read_bit()`, `od_ec_decode_bool_q15()` branches on poisoned `dif` and MSan reports the crash at `aom_dsp/entdec.c:176`. The patch resolves this exact obligation by adding both missing tile-column bounds checks in `get_ls_tile_buffers()` before the decoder trusts either the header width or the derived column end.

tainted_value_origin.description: First concrete tainted length. This statement reinterprets raw tile-group bytes as the current tile-column length, which is then trusted to derive `tile_col_data_end[c]` and the later out-of-range tile buffer span.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `get_ls_tile_buffers()` trusts the attacker-decoded tile-column size and advances `tile_col_data_end[c]` without proving the derived column end still lies within the real tile-group buffer.
root_cause.note: The patch adds both missing obligations in this block: a pre-read `tile_col_size_bytes > data_end - data` guard before `mem_get_varsize()` and a post-read `tile_col_size > (size_t)(data_end - data)` guard before `tile_col_data_end[c] = data + tile_col_size`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is closed from the staged source, patch, reproduction report, and saved sanitizer traces only.

The staged vulnerable checkout at `gt_results/arvo_42533480/_work/src/aom` is on commit `cae8fbe572bec3443b89d9be858ff0abb7020f1b`, not metadata commit `cc9e46cb0da9323ecacf679772f6f5b21934a363`. All line anchors below are resolved against the staged checkout because that is the exact source snapshot used for Stage 01 reproduction.

The saved artifacts prove that the crash consumed heap-origin uninitialized bytes and that the fix hunk adds the missing tile-column bounds checks, but they do not expose the exact numeric `tile_col_size_bytes` or `tile_col_size` values inside the witness. The trace therefore stays at the exact source-level obligations added by `patch.diff` rather than guessing specific field values.

coarse_trace.summary: Frame-header parsing enters the large-scale ext-tile path and materializes attacker-controlled `tile_col_size_bytes` and `tile_size_bytes`.
Tile-group parsing reads a non-last column length from attacker bytes and, without the patch's bounds checks, derives `tile_col_data_end[c]` beyond the real `data_end`.
Per-tile parsing trusts that bogus column bound, records an out-of-range `tile_buffer`, and initializes a worker `aom_reader` from it because `read_is_valid` does not reject `data > data_end`.
Entropy-decoder refill mixes bytes from the out-of-range buffer into `dec->dif`; MemorySanitizer attributes those bytes to the uninitialized heap allocation in `alloc_dec_jobs`.
Coefficient-sign decoding consumes the poisoned reader state and MSan reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `od_ec_decode_bool_q15`.

fine_trace.note: Source. In the large-scale ext-tile frame-header path, attacker-controlled bits materialize the widths of the later tile-column and per-tile size fields.

For each non-last tile column, the decoder reinterprets `tile_col_size_bytes` bytes from the tile-group payload as `tile_col_size`. Vulnerable code does this before proving that enough bytes remain in `[data, data_end)` for that width.

Root cause. After step 2, vulnerable code trusts the decoded `tile_col_size` and advances the column end pointer without checking `tile_col_size > (size_t)(data_end - data)`. Combined with the missing width check from step 2, `tile_col_data_end[c]` can land past the real tile-group `data_end`, and later code uses that out-of-range pointer as the column-local bound.

Because the caller passes `tile_col_data_end[c]` from step 3 as this function's `data_end`, the size check is evaluated against the bogus column bound rather than the real tile-group end. The function can therefore accept a tile span whose `*data` / `size` lie past the actual payload and records that out-of-range span in `tile_buffers[row][col]`.
The row-mt worker seeds its boolean decoder from the `tile_buffer` selected in step 4. On the crashing run, this happens on the saved `row_mt_worker_hook -> parse_tile_row_mt` path.

The only validation here is `read_is_valid(data, read_size, data_end)`, and `read_is_valid()` is implemented as `len != 0 && len <= (size_t)(end - start)`. When step 4 has already produced `data > data_end`, the signed difference underflows in the cast to `size_t`, so the check does not reject the out-of-range span and `aom_reader_init()` initializes the entropy reader on it.

The arithmetic decoder now reads a byte through `bptr[0]` from the out-of-range buffer accepted in step 6 and folds it into `dif`; the updated value is later stored back into `dec->dif` at line 112. On the saved run, MemorySanitizer traces these bytes to the uninitialized heap allocation in `alloc_dec_jobs()` at `av1/decoder/decodeframe.c:3339`.

Later, while the row-mt worker decodes transform coefficients, `av1_read_coeffs_txb()` consumes the same poisoned `aom_reader` to read a coefficient-sign bit. The saved crash stack reaches `od_ec_decode_bool_q15()` through this `aom_read_bit()` call.

Sink. `aom_read_bit()` reaches `od_ec_decode_bool_q15()`, which branches on local `dif` loaded from decoder state. Because step 7 seeded that state from out-of-range, uninitialized heap bytes, MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this predicate.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan origin says the poisoned bytes were created by this heap allocation: `CHECK_MEM_ERROR(cm, tile_mt_info->job_queue, aom_malloc(sizeof(*tile_mt_info->job_queue) * num_tiles));`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_summary: MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value in od_ec_decode_bool_q15 at /src/aom/aom_dsp/entdec.c:176:7; the stack includes aom_read_, aom_read_bit_, av1_read_coeffs_txb, av1_read_coeffs_txb_facade, decode_token_recon_block, decode_partition, and parse_tile_row_mt/row_mt_worker_hook, matching OSS-Fuzz issue 42533480.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context explains where the poisoned bytes lived on the saved run (`job_queue` from `alloc_dec_jobs`), while the patchable source-level bug is earlier: `get_ls_tile_buffers()` fails to bound-check the tile-column size read and derived `tile_col_data_end[c]` before later code treats that out-of-range region as bitstream input.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved run `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42533480 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `od_ec_decode_bool_q15` while `av1_dec_fuzzer` processed `poc`.

format.contract: Grounded only for the exact 160-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42533480/poc` with sha256 `e8a65d22f51e98259636af4a4f2e7eeb8eff6639cb6e7630d06b742a235ca325`. Stage 02 source analysis establishes only that this exact file reaches the large-scale ext-tile path, materializes attacker-controlled `tile_col_size_bytes` / `tile_size_bytes`, and later supplies tile-column size bytes that make `get_ls_tile_buffers()` trust a column end beyond the real tile-group payload. The saved artifacts do not establish the exact numeric header values, so this contract must not be generalized to broader AV1 inputs.
